system_type_reason: Low-code framework for assembling LLM applications from flows and modules.

repo_overview.summary: Low-code framework for assembling multi-agent LLM applications from flows (Pipeline, Parallel, Loop, Switch, Graph) and modules (online models, locally deployed or fine-tunable models). Agents are one component type: ReactAgent wraps a single FunctionCall step (LLM reasoning plus tool execution) in a bounded loop; PlanAndSolve and ReWOO variants add planner/solver stages. Large surrounding tool areas cover RAG, data synthesis pipelines, file systems, services and a multi-round LLM code-review runner.

prompters, output formatters, deploy backends (vllm, lightllm, ...) and finetune backends
module abstraction: ModuleBase, ServerModule, TrainableModule, online model adapters per provider and dynamic router (llms/onlinemodule/)
agent core: base class, FunctionCall step, ReactAgent, PlanAndSolveAgent, ReWOOAgent, ToolManager, skills, shell/file/todo tools, code interpreter
MCP client integration for external tools
git platform clients and a multi-round LLM code-review runner with checkpoints, lint and coverage checks
RAG stack: document loading, parsing, stores, retrievers, rerankers; doc_service and parsing_service run ingestion as a service with a SQL-backed task queue and worker processes
LLM-driven data synthesis and cleaning operators and pipelines
file system abstractions, server wrappers, train/infer services, web UI, evaluation
LightEngine building executable graphs from JSON descriptions
tracing subsystem with backends, collection and consumption

topology.justification: The agent abstraction is one LLM driving one tool loop: ReactAgent wraps FunctionCall in loop(...) with a stop condition (reactAgent.py:109). PlanAndSolveAgent and ReWOOAgent share plan and solve LLM instances inside a fixed pipeline; only the solver runs the FunctionCall tool loop, the planner is a single prompt step of the same workflow (planAndSolveAgent.py:57-61). The git review application creates several independent ReactAgent instances per file or review unit (e.g. ragent_verify.py:269-277); fixed Python stage code decides which agent runs and collects their results. The engine's FunctionCall node accepts arbitrary engine nodes as tools (engine.py:501-506), so nesting agents is possible only through a user-defined graph.

resilience.name: ReAct loop iteration cap
resilience.what_it_is: The FunctionCall step runs inside loop(..., count=max_retries + 1) with max_retries defaulting to 5, so at most 6 LLM/tool rounds. If the loop ends with a pending tool-call dict and no text answer, _post_process raises ValueError. PlanAndSolveAgent applies the same cap to each solver sub-loop and FunctionCallAgent to its loop.
resilience.function_in_system: Bounds the outer agent loop in ReactAgent.build_agent. Stops runaway tool-calling where the model keeps requesting tools and never produces a final answer. Otherwise a looping model burns unbounded tokens, time and tool side effects.

resilience.name: forced final summary on iteration exhaustion
resilience.what_it_is: With force_summarize=True, hitting the iteration cap triggers one extra non-streaming LLM call. It receives the last 8 history messages (content cut to 300 chars, 1000 for the newest), an optional task context of up to 500 chars and the instruction to stop calling tools and answer immediately. Its text replaces the ValueError; if the call fails or returns nothing, the ValueError is raised as before.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in ReactAgent._post_process after the loop has run out of iterations. Converts a hard failure into a best-effort answer built from the tool observations gathered so far. Otherwise the caller receives only an exception and all intermediate work is lost.

resilience.name: compaction of old tool results in chat history
resilience.what_it_is: With keep_full_turns=N > 0, the chat history passed to the LLM keeps the newest N tool-result messages intact and truncates every older tool result to its first 200 characters, prefixed with a '[truncated X chars]' marker.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in FunctionCall._build_history before every LLM call. Keeps the prompt size in check during long tool chains with large observations. Otherwise the history grows with every full tool output until it hits the context window or inflates cost per turn.

resilience.name: tool-call validation with error feedback to the model
resilience.what_it_is: ToolManager checks every tool call for a valid structure, a known tool name and arguments that pass the pydantic schema generated from the tool signature and docstring. Each failure yields an error string as the tool result (e.g. 'Tool [x] is not available. Please choose from the available tools.'). Exceptions raised inside a tool are caught and returned as '[Tool Error] <Type>: <msg>'. MCP tool wrappers apply the same pattern: missing required parameters and failed MCP calls return an error string.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the LLM output and tool execution in FunctionCall._post_action. Hallucinated tools, malformed arguments and crashing tools become observations the model reads in the next round and can correct. Otherwise one bad tool call raises out of the loop and aborts the whole agent run.

resilience.name: lenient tool-argument parsing and text fallback for tool calls
resilience.what_it_is: Tool arguments are parsed with json5; on failure trailing commas are stripped, and as a last resort a truncated JSON is trimmed and closed by appending the missing brackets and braces. If the LLM output carries no structured tool_calls, a regex recognizes free text of the form 'Action: Call <tool> with parameters {...}' and turns it into a tool call.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the parsing boundary between LLM output and ToolManager. Salvages slightly malformed or truncated model output (e.g. output cut off at the token limit, models that write tool calls as text). Otherwise such turns end the loop as a plain-text 'final answer' or fail argument parsing.

resilience.name: history reset after a failed step
resilience.what_it_is: If a FunctionCall step raises, the per-session agent workspace and the LLM chat history are cleared before the exception propagates.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in FunctionCall.forward around the LLM plus tool pipeline. Per the code comment, it keeps a follow-up request (e.g. the user saying 'continue') from inheriting a corrupted history with truncated tool_calls and invalid JSON arguments. Otherwise every later turn in the session replays the broken messages and fails again.

resilience.name: dangerous-action guard in builtin tools
resilience.what_it_is: shell_tool matches the command against a denylist (rm -rf, sudo, chmod, kill, package managers, curl/wget/ssh, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, output redirection). write_file on an existing file, delete_file, move_file and download_file are gated as well. A hit returns {'status': 'needs_approval', 'reason': ...} and the action is skipped. An optional root argument confines file paths to a directory. The gate is lifted by the allow_unsafe parameter, which is part of the tool schema exposed to the LLM; no code in the repo routes needs_approval to a human.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the builtin tools that every agent receives by default (enable_builtin_tools=True). Blocks the first attempt at a destructive or network action and tells the model why. The model can re-issue the call with allow_unsafe=True, so the guard is a speed bump that the model itself controls. Otherwise a single hallucinated command deletes files, installs packages or leaks data with no friction at all. Skill scripts started through run_script pass through the same shell_tool check.

resilience.name: execution and output bounds for builtin tools
resilience.what_it_is: Default limits on builtin tools: shell_tool subprocess timeout 30 s, download_file timeout 30 s, read_file returns at most 200000 chars and flags truncated=True, search_in_files stops at 50 matches and skips files over 2 MB, get_skill rejects SKILL.md files over 5 MB (config max_skill_md_bytes) with status 'too_large'.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the tool implementations, below ToolManager. Keeps a single tool call from hanging the loop or dumping a huge observation into the next prompt. Otherwise a stuck command blocks the agent indefinitely and a large file or search result floods the context window.

resilience.name: credential-based tool hiding and first-valid provider fallback
resilience.what_it_is: Tools or groups registered with a key_source (env var, config entry, globals entry or callable) are dropped from the tool descriptions when none of their keys resolves (should_skip). A group with pick_first_valid=True exposes only its first child whose key is available, forming an ordered fallback chain across tool providers.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in tool description generation before each LLM call. The model only sees tools that can actually run with the current credentials, and a provider group degrades to the next configured provider. Otherwise the model picks tools that fail with auth errors and wastes turns on them.

resilience.name: model-call retry with fixed delay schedule
resilience.what_it_is: Online chat calls and TrainableModule calls are retried on requests exceptions (ConnectionError, ChunkedEncodingError and any RequestException, which includes every non-200 HTTP status) up to max_retries=3 attempts, sleeping 3 s, 10 s, 30 s between attempts. All error classes are retried alike, auth and bad-request errors included.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the HTTP request inside the LLM module's forward, one level below the FunctionCall step. Absorbs transient network drops and provider hiccups before they surface as a failed agent step. Otherwise a single dropped connection raises through FunctionCall and ends the agent run.

resilience.name: continuation of interrupted streaming responses
resilience.what_it_is: When a stream breaks mid-response, the content received so far is extracted. On the retry the online module appends it as an assistant message plus a user message asking the model to continue exactly where it left off with no repetition. If the cut happened inside a tool_calls block, the continuation is skipped and the original messages are resent, since truncated function arguments trigger 400 errors at providers. TrainableModule appends the partial output to the original input for the retry.
resilience.function_in_system: Part of the retry loop of the LLM module. Preserves already generated tokens across a connection drop, saving time and output cost on long responses. Otherwise every interruption restarts generation from scratch.

resilience.name: module result cache
resilience.what_it_is: ModuleBase.use_cache() enables caching of a module's forward result keyed by an md5 hash of args and kwargs. Storage backends: memory (default), file, sqlite, redis (LAZYLLM_CACHE_STRATEGY); LAZYLLM_CACHE_MODE selects RW, RO, WO or NONE. The config flag cache_local_module turns it on for all TrainableModules and is described as intended for unit tests.

Otherwise identical requests (e.g. repeated test or development runs) pay for a full model call each time.

resilience.name: model backend fallback chain and key-based provider selection at construction
resilience.what_it_is: AutoModel tries, in order: a TrainableModule bound to a deployed endpoint from config, an OnlineModule from config, a plain OnlineModule, and finally a local TrainableModule; each failure is logged and the next stage is tried. When OnlineChatModule is created with no source, it picks the configured default source or else the first registered provider whose *_api_key is set.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs once when the application wires up its LLM, before any agent loop starts. Lets the same code come up on whatever backend is available in the current environment. Otherwise a missing deployment or missing key for one provider aborts application startup.

resilience.name: random spreading across multiple API keys and base URLs
resilience.what_it_is: If api_key or base_url is given as a list, each request picks one entry via random.choice. Selection is uniform and ignores past failures.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in header and URL resolution of every online model request. Spreads load and per-key rate limits across several keys or endpoints. Otherwise all traffic hits one key or endpoint and runs into its rate limit sooner.

resilience.name: subprocess sandbox with timeout for tool execution
resilience.what_it_is: DummySandbox writes the code to a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp directory, runs it as a separate Python process with the temp dir as cwd, kills it after timeout=30 s and removes the directory in a finally block. ToolManager serializes every registered tool with execute_in_sandbox=True (the ModuleTool default) and its arguments via cloudpickle into a script and runs that script in the sandbox; builtin tools set execute_in_sandbox=False. SandboxFusion is a remote backend selectable via SANDBOX_TYPE with run_timeout, compile_timeout, memory_limit_mb and a ping check before first use.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in ToolManager.forward between tool-call validation and tool execution. Hanging tools are stopped after 30 s, crashes and file side effects stay inside a child process and a throwaway directory. On the ToolManager path the sandbox returns only result.stderr on failure, so a timeout or blocked script reaches the model as an empty observation. Otherwise a user tool that hangs or crashes blocks or kills the agent process itself.

resilience.name: progressive skill disclosure
resilience.what_it_is: SkillManager builds a skill index from the YAML front matter (name, description) of each SKILL.md, skipping files above max_skill_md_bytes (5 MB), unreadable files and invalid metadata. The system prompt lists only names and descriptions; the full SKILL.md is loaded on demand through the get_skill tool. The prompt requires get_skill before read_reference/run_script and demands rel_path values copied verbatim from SKILL.md; the code checks only that the path exists.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in system-prompt construction and in the skill tools of the agent. Only the skill instructions relevant to the current task enter the context, and the path rule targets hallucinated script and reference paths. Otherwise every installed skill body is loaded into every prompt, or the model guesses file paths and runs arbitrary scripts.

evidence.snippet:
### How to Use Skills (Progressive Disclosure)
You can see the name/description above, but only fetch a skill's full instructions when it's relevant.

1) **Identify relevance**: If a skill's description matches the task, consider using it.
2) **Get the skill's full usage**: Call `get_skill` to retrieve the complete workflow.

**Prerequisite**: You MUST call `get_skill` for the skill first and receive its
SKILL.md content before you can use `read_reference` or `run_script`.

**Path Rule**: The `rel_path` argument MUST be copied verbatim from the SKILL.md
body. You are FORBIDDEN from fabricating, guessing, or extrapolating paths.

resilience.name: stage checkpointing with resume and invalidation
resilience.what_it_is: The PR review pipeline stores every stage result and a done flag per stage in a per-PR JSON checkpoint, flushed to disk on each save. resume_from=<stage> marks that stage and all later ones as invalid, a higher _PIPELINE_VERSION discards the whole checkpoint, and a changed head sha backs up the old file and purges all diff-dependent data while keeping CLONE, ARCH and SPEC. UPLOAD is skipped only on an explicit done flag.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps every stage of the git review runner. After a crash, timeout or failed comment upload the next run continues at the first missing stage and reuses all finished LLM and agent rounds, and the upload stage avoids double posting. Otherwise every interruption repeats the full multi-round review and its LLM cost.

Otherwise one throttled or cut-off answer aborts the review run or crashes the stage parser.

def _truncate_diff_at_file_boundary(diff_text: str, max_chars: int) -> tuple:
    # Truncate diff at a clean file boundary instead of mid-file.
    # Returns (truncated_diff, was_truncated).
    # Finds the last "diff --git" header that starts before max_chars,
    # and cuts just before it if including that file would exceed the limit.
    import re
    file_starts = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r'^diff --git ', diff_text, re.MULTILINE)]
    if not file_starts:
        return diff_text[:max_chars] + '\n... [diff truncated]\n', True

resilience.name: deployment readiness check with automatic job restart
resilience.what_it_is: When a locally deployed model server (vLLM, LMDeploy, LightLLM, Infinity, MindIE) starts, verify_func tails the job log queue. A startup line such as 'Uvicorn running on' marks the job ready; an error line ('ERROR:'), a Failed job status or 600 s without a startup line count as failure. Job.start(restart=3) then stops the job, waits 2 s and restarts it up to three times before raising a RuntimeError with the last log lines. Kubernetes jobs use restart_policy='OnFailure' with backoff_limit=3.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in model deployment, before any agent calls the model. Catches servers that crash or hang during startup and restarts them. Otherwise the agent is wired to a dead endpoint and the failure surfaces only at the first LLM call inside the loop.

resilience.name: transient-error retry with exponential backoff in RAG ingestion
resilience.what_it_is: retry_transient retries only errors whose message or type name matches a list of transient patterns (Connection, Timeout, SSLEOFError, Too Many Requests, Bad Gateway, rate limit, ...) and re-raises all others immediately. The delay grows as base_delay ** (attempt + 1), i.e. 2, 4, 8 s, for up to 3 retries. An on_retry hook resets the embedding state of the affected nodes. The generic @retry decorator (3 attempts, fixed delay) wraps PDF loading.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around batch embedding in parallel_do_embedding and around each PDF split sent to the MinerU and PaddleOCR services during document ingestion for retrieval. Absorbs network hiccups and rate limits of embedding and OCR backends. Otherwise one transient error aborts indexing of a whole document and leaves the knowledge base incomplete.

resilience.name: lease-based task claiming with renewal and stale-task recovery in the parsing worker
resilience.what_it_is: Parsing workers claim tasks from a SQL-backed queue with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and receive a lease (default 300 s). A daemon thread extends the lease every 60 s while the task runs. claim() also takes over WORKING tasks whose lease has expired. On worker start, _cleanup_stale_tasks resets expired WORKING queue entries to WAITING and marks orphaned WORKING node-group status rows as FAILED.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the document parsing service that ingests and indexes documents for RAG retrieval, around each task execution in _run_task. Recovers from crashed or hung workers by returning their tasks to the queue for another worker. Otherwise a worker crash leaves documents stuck in WORKING forever and they never reach the knowledge base.
